record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; notebooks and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal-rate results for a weight-modified model, testing the practical-removal version, but does not report the original activation-ablation method.
record.gate_note: The README reports saved refusal rates. It does not specify that the edited direction was computed as the harmful-minus-harmless difference in means. The ASR heuristic counts long non-refusal responses and is explicitly not a check of whether an answer is harmful, so it is not recorded as a refusal result. The README notes that the runs used different prompt sets and had some training/evaluation overlap.
record.test_reason: The study applies a weight edit (notebook '04_orthogonalize_save') to Llama 3.2 1B, a model outside the original source. It reports keyword refusal rates before and after the edit in two runtimes, which bears on V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The README says the modified model has reduced refusal behavior. It cautions that the saved metrics are run results rather than a precise safety measure, because of keyword-based refusal, a length-only ASR heuristic, differing prompt sets, and train/eval overlap.
record.recipe_differences: Repository project/tool, not a stated replication. The README describes activation extraction, direction screening, and weight modification, but does not specify the direction formula or report the original activation-projection procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says the runs used different prompt sets and had some training/evaluation overlap.
record.problems: The README says the runs used different prompt sets with some training/evaluation overlap. Refusal is keyword-based; the ASR heuristic does not check harmfulness. No uncertainty estimates or general-capability results are reported, and the model workflow was not rerun as part of the cleanup.
record.rows_left_out: The table's ASR heuristic values were not recorded as rows because they count long non-refusal responses rather than measuring actual harmfulness or refusal directly.

untested.parts: Retention of general capabilities after the edit. Whether the edited direction is the difference-in-means direction. Harmfulness of outputs, since ASR is only a length heuristic.
Activation ablation, direction addition to induce refusal, and capability retention. Not reported in the README.

record.verdict_notes: This is an unreviewed GitHub project with 0 stars. Only the README and file list were available; docs/results.md and the notebooks were not read and may hold more details, such as the direction choice and layer. The evidence is weak: there is no uncertainty, no capability check, and the baseline is not matched. The persistence of refusal after conversion to GGUF/Ollama (35% versus 33.75%) suggests the edit survives format conversion.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not identify a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, report activation projection at every layer and position, test adding the direction, or measure retained general abilities.
The README reports weight-modified model results, but does not establish that these are released models produced by the specific ablation procedure in the claim.
Jailbreak suppression and robustness training are not reported.
No comparison of a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
Separate encoding of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is not tested.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct stages is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.
